analysis: external metrics phase 1: prediction MAE vs historical-mean baseline; phase 2: selection quality under a fixed inspection budget; phase 3: Race (guided vs random selection, model vs historical-mean prediction); phase 4B: T7 prediction (NASA, Apache) through the existing validation adapters; phase 4C: Cars T7 prediction adapters; phase 5C: Fix observed alternatives (Cars, Apache); phase 5D: Justify truthfulness; phase 5E: Remember shortlist quality; phase 5F: Certify agreement with the frozen statistical oracle; phase 5G: Flow streaming quality
status: post-observation (added after the Task Talk; not pre-registered)

protocol.held_out: rows whose 1-based number is divisible by 5 (harness.oracle.held_out)
protocol.baseline: mean target of the non-held-out rows, scored on the held-out rows
protocol.metric: mae_ratio = model_mae / baseline_mae; undefined (excluded) when baseline_mae == 0
protocol.beats_baseline: model_mae < baseline_mae (strict, as in the frozen checker)
protocol.primary_inclusion: program ran; ANSWER accepted by harness.answers.check_request; mask leakage rerun recorded as passed
protocol.leakage_unverified_policy: excluded from primary (analysis choice, documented in the report)

selection.answer: ANSWER <ID> {"order": [row numbers, first evaluated first]}; 10..budget distinct rows (validated by harness.answers.check_request)
selection.candidate_pool: every row of the domain CSV (1-based file order)
selection.budget: harness.oracle.budget(n) = min(30, n // 5): cars 30, nasa 18, apache 30
selection.score: harness.oracle.d2h over all rows (min-max bounds over all rows, goal direction from the column suffix); lower is better; used only to grade rows the program already listed
selection.best_d2h: lowest d2h among the rows in the recorded order
selection.regret: best_d2h - lowest d2h in the candidate pool
selection.normalized_regret: regret / (highest - lowest d2h in the pool); undefined when that range is 0
selection.expected_random_best: exact expectation of the lowest d2h among k rows drawn uniformly without replacement, k = number of rows in the order (no simulated draws)
selection.p_random_at_least_as_good: probability that k random rows include one with d2h <= best_d2h
selection.common_k: the same metrics on the first 10 rows of every order (the minimum length allowed), for comparison across domains and order lengths
selection.primary_inclusion: program ran; ANSWER accepted by harness.answers.check_request; honeypot rerun recorded as passed

race.note: NASA-19 is the prediction race and NASA-20 the selection race; Cars and Apache are the other way round

selection.answer: {"budget": b, "repeats": >= 20, "ours": [best row per repeat], "random": [best of b random rows per repeat], "verdict": ...}; schema validated by harness.answers.check_request
selection.score: harness.oracle.d2h over all rows of the CSV (lower is better)
selection.empirical: archived per-repeat rows of both arms: medians, median_advantage = median random d2h - median guided d2h (positive = guided better), win_fraction = repeats where guided d2h < random d2h (pairs taken by repeat index as recorded)
selection.analytical: expected_random_best = exact expected best d2h of `budget` rows drawn uniformly without replacement from all rows; advantage_vs_analytic = expected_random_best - median guided d2h
selection.primary_inclusion: program ran; schema valid; honeypot rerun passed; reported budget == harness.oracle.budget(n)
selection.empirical_inclusion: primary and the frozen check 'random baseline is really random' passed on the base run
selection.unverifiable: the rows each arm evaluated are not archived, so it cannot be checked that `ours` and `random` are really the best of what each arm saw

prediction.metric: same definitions as phase 1 (every-fifth-row hold-out, training-mean baseline, mae_ratio)
prediction.verification: model and baseline MAE recomputed from the recorded predictions and the CSV; the program's reported baseline, mae_model and mae_baseline are compared (rel. 0.5%, 1%, 1% as the frozen checker does) but never used
prediction.primary_inclusion: program ran; schema valid; mask leakage rerun passed
prediction.separate_from_phase1: the Guess request (skill 2) and the Race request (skill 10) are never pooled

t7_prediction.identity: T7: one human-directed implementation per domain; deterministic; not an LLM trial
t7_prediction.protocol: v2-common: every-fifth-row hold-out, training-mean baseline (t7_validation adapter)
t7_prediction.execution: each adapter is run locally with the current Python (-B, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1) on the domain CSV; harness.semantic.evaluate reruns it on its shuffled, mask and (Race) honeypot copies in temporary directories; evidence is kept in memory and hashed, never written to t7_validation/results
t7_prediction.scoring: same functions as phases 1 and 3: baseline, model_mae, mae_ratio on harness.oracle.held_out rows
t7_prediction.inclusion: same as T1-T6: ran; ANSWER accepted by harness.answers.check_request; mask leakage rerun passed
t7_prediction.comparison: descriptive only; T7 is n = 1 per domain, so same()/bestRanks are not applied
t7_prediction.development_note: the T7 adapters were written and refined against the common semantic checker; T1-T6 programs were generated one-shot without access to it

foundation.cars: human-directed scripts on the shared shrinking_code library, which was developed with LLM assistance (README, Disclosure); the library is not independently human-written

t7_prediction.evaluated_requests: NASA/Apache: both requests of the step; Cars: the prediction request only

fix.status: post-hoc (added after the Task Talk); every rule below is an analysis choice unless it quotes the frozen checker
fix.nature: all four measurable requests pick an EXISTING row of the CSV as the alternative; the improvement is the difference between two recorded rows, not the effect of changing a vehicle or server
fix.visibility: Fix is retrospective: every goal value is visible to the program by design, so there is no hidden target and no leakage gate; only the shuffled rerun applies (recorded, not gating)
fix.integrity_valid: ran; ANSWER accepted by harness.answers.check_request; every cited [from, to] cell value matches the file (no fabricated values)
fix.CAR-15: score = harness.oracle.d2h (lower is better). observed_improvement = d2h(row) - d2h(best listed alternative). similar = among the 25% most similar rows (harness.oracle.XSpace.nearest, the frozen check). success = row in the worse half by d2h and >= 1 listed alternative both better by d2h and similar
fix.CAR-16: targets are the program's own thresholds (frozen format). success = targets within the observed range, the row misses >= 1 target, the alternative meets more targets, and it changes no more input columns than the minimum over all rows meeting more targets (min_changes, computed from the CSV)
fix.APACHE-15: observed_improvement = Performance-(row) - Performance-(alternative) (positive = faster). best_possible_improvement = the largest such improvement over rows differing in 1-2 settings; improvement_captured = observed / best possible (blank when the best possible is <= 0). success = row in the worse half, alternative differs in 1-2 settings, observed_improvement > 0
fix.APACHE-16: target is the program's own value (frozen format). gap_reduction = |row - target| - |alternative - target|. success = target better than the row and in range, alternative closer to it, and no more changed settings than the minimum over all rows closer to the target
fix.NASA-15/16: not independently measurable: NASA-15/16 answers report predicted effort/defects after a hypothetical change; no observed outcome exists for the changed project, so the improvement cannot be verified
fix.reported_values: APACHE-15 performance.before/after are compared with the recorded values, never used

justify.status: post-hoc (added after the Task Talk); success rules are analysis choices unless they repeat a frozen checker rule
justify.integrity_valid: ran; ANSWER accepted by harness.answers.check_request; every cited cell value (neighbour values, pair differences) matches the file
justify.justify_pair: true trade-offs T = goals where the non-preferred row is strictly better (direction from the column suffix; ties are not trade-offs). Claimed C = the answer's `tradeoffs`. precision = |C&T|/|C| (blank if C empty), recall = |C&T|/|T| (blank if T empty), exact = C == T, false_claims = |C-T|, omissions = |T-C|. success = exact, preferred not dominated, every cited difference real and really different, scores rank the preferred row higher, and (CAR-12, frozen 'different strengths' rule) T non-empty
justify.justify_neighbors: subject = recommended row; d2h percentile = share of rows with strictly lower d2h (0 = best); good = Pareto-optimal or best 25% by any aggregate (frozen rule); neighbour similarity = among the 25% most similar rows by harness.oracle.XSpace (frozen rule) and the mean share of rows strictly closer. success = subject good and every neighbour similar
justify.justify_estimate: NASA-11: one held-out project; error |estimate - actual Effort-| and the training-mean error on that row. No mask rerun exists for this request, so leakage cannot be ruled out; the error is reported, not used for success. success = project held out, neighbours not held out and similar, estimate within [0.5 min, 2 max] of neighbour efforts (frozen rule)
justify.meaning: these check that explanations are truthful about recorded rows; they are not human-rated usefulness and not evidence that any change would cause an improvement

remember.status: post-hoc (added after the Task Talk); success uses the frozen checker's own -02 rules
remember.integrity_valid: ran and ANSWER accepted by harness.answers.check_request; the -02 answers cite only row numbers and computed shares, so there are no cited cell values to verify; shuffled rerun recorded, not gating
remember.-01: summary fidelity only (share of the per-goal mean/median/min/max/best/worst values that are correct, as the frozen checker computes them); it is a description of the data, not an external recommendation metric
remember.CAR-02/NASA-02: truth = Pareto front under the goal directions (harness.oracle.pareto). precision = hits/k, recall = hits/|front|, recall_attainable = hits/min(k, |front|), base_rate = |front|/n. percentile = share of rows with strictly lower d2h (0 = best). success (frozen rule) = at least 8 of 10 rows Pareto-optimal or in the best 25% by any aggregate, and the list is not just the top rows of one goal
remember.APACHE-02: truth = best quartile of observed Performance- (harness.oracle.best_fraction, ties included; the 25% cut is the frozen checker's). precision = hits/k, recall = hits/|quartile|, percentile = share of rows with strictly lower Performance-. settings_accuracy = share of listed settings whose top_share and rest_share are within 0.011 of the truth (frozen tolerance). success (frozen rules) = at least 80% of the listed rows in the best quartile, every listed share correct, and the first setting among the two most distinguishing
remember.top_10: precision_at_10 uses the first 10 listed rows and is reported only when k >= 10
remember.meaning: Pareto non-domination and best-quartile performance follow from the declared goals and recorded values; they are not verified customer preferences, prices or satisfaction

certify.status: post-hoc (added after the Task Talk); the reference decision is the frozen oracle's own rule
certify.what_it_measures: agreement of each program's 'different'/'same' verdicts with harness.oracle.clear_verdict on the same groups; this is oracle consistency, not real-world effect detection and not an A/A false-alarm rate (no repeated same-treatment measurements exist in the archive)
certify.reference: harness.oracle.clear_verdict(xs, ys): 'different' when |Cliff's delta| >= 0.474 and the two-sample KS test rejects at 95% (critical 1.36*sqrt((n+m)/(nm))); 'same' when |delta| < 0.147 and KS does not reject; otherwise undecidable (either verdict accepted). Groups under 5 rows are never decidable. Thresholds are the frozen oracle's; none are added
certify.groups (CAR-05, NASA-05/06, APACHE-05/06: groups = every distinct value of the group column, members = rows with a recorded outcome (as the frozen checker forms them); one reference per unordered pair; when a pair is listed twice the last listing counts (as in the checker)
certify.year_groups (CAR-06): groups = the program's own two Model ranges (rows with from <= Model <= to). One reference per overall score (d2h, zsum, ranksum; lower = better). The comparison is decidable only when all three are decidable and agree; if any is undecidable, or they conflict, the frozen checker accepts either verdict and the comparison is counted as undecidable
certify.outcomes: agree; false_positive = said 'different' where the oracle says 'same'; false_negative = said 'same' where the oracle says 'different'; undecidable_said_same / undecidable_said_different = verdicts on pairs the oracle cannot decide (both accepted; 'same' there is the schema's 'not reliably different')
certify.abstention: the frozen schema allows only 'different' or 'same'; any other label (for example 'inconclusive') is a schema error, recorded as schema_error_type = verdict_label with the label in abstention_label; a skipped pair is schema_error_type = missing_comparison
certify.agreement_rate: agree / n_decidable within one answer; blank when the answer has no decidable comparison. Comparisons inside one program are not independent trials; cells report the median over trials and pooled counts only as descriptive totals
certify.oracle_consistent: schema-valid and no false positive or false negative (vacuously true when nothing is decidable; n_decidable shows when)
certify.direction: for oracle-'different' pairs of the groups kind: does the order of the reported group means favour the same group as the oracle (sign of Cliff's delta under the outcome's goal direction)? The schema has no effect-size field, so effect-size error is not measurable; group n/median/mean accuracy is reported instead (median within the checker's tolerance of any median, mean within O.close)
certify.frozen_base_pass: every base check of harness.answers.check_request passes (group statistics and verdicts)
certify.integrity_valid: ran and ANSWER accepted by the frozen format check; the answers cite computed group statistics, not row values, so there are no fabricated cells to gate on; archived shuffled-rerun verdict failures are recorded, not gating

flow.status: post-hoc (added after the Task Talk); arrival order, checkpoints and thresholds are the frozen ones, and every reference set is computed from rows that have already arrived
flow.request_mapping: frozen kinds: CAR-07 stream_desirable; NASA-07 stream_alert_pred (per-arrival effort/defect predictions and alerts); APACHE-07 stream_alert_poor; CAR-08, NASA-08, APACHE-08 stream_summary (checkpoint summaries and a 5-row shortlist). NASA-08 has no alerts
flow.arrivals: harness.oracle.arrivals: the last round(0.2 n) rows in file order; the rows before are history. At arrival r the visible rows are 1..r (r's own recorded columns are in the file the program reads)
flow.CAR-07: decision = desirable. Reference (post-hoc application of the oracle's own 'best seen' set, the one the frozen stream_summary checker uses): r in harness.oracle.good_rows(data, 0.25, rows 1..r) — Pareto-optimal or in the best 25% under any aggregate among rows seen so far. Strict reference: r on the Pareto front of rows 1..r. Precision = tp/(tp+fp), recall = tp/(tp+fn); blank with no decisions/positives. Labels a record whose goals are already observed: classification of observed records, not prediction
flow.NASA-07 predictions: MAE of predicted_effort against the recorded Effort-; baseline = mean Effort- of rows 1..r-1 (history plus earlier arrivals only); mae_ratio = model/baseline; better_than_baseline_share = arrivals with |pred - actual| < |baseline - actual|; the same for predicted_defects. Self-reported statistics are not used. self_match_share = predictions within O.close of the arrival's own recorded Effort- (a post-hoc indicator of self-leakage, which the frozen future rerun cannot detect because it changes only later arrivals)
flow.NASA-07 alerts: post-hoc application of the frozen alert-justification threshold to actual outcomes: an arrival is high when its recorded Effort- or Defects- exceeds the median of rows 1..r-1. Prospective: the alert is supposed to come from predictions made before the outcome is known
flow.APACHE-07: rule adherence, not prediction: the alert is raised after the arrival's Performance- is observed. Positive = worse than the median of rows 1..r-1 (the frozen justification threshold); must_alert = worse than every earlier row (the frozen required alert)
flow.-08 checkpoints: after m = 0, k//2, k arrivals, visible rows 1..history+m. summary fidelity = share of per-goal n/mean/min/max values correct; future_rows_used = shortlisted rows not yet arrived (leakage); good_precision = shortlisted rows in O.good_rows(data, 0.25, visible) / 5 (frozen pass needs >= 4/5); front_precision = rows on the Pareto front of visible rows / 5; percentile = share of visible rows with strictly lower d2h (bounds from visible rows); arrivals_shortlisted and good_arrivals_available show whether new arrivals were incorporated
flow.integrity_valid: ran, ANSWER accepted by the frozen format check, and for -07 the archived future rerun passed (fail = earlier decisions changed when only later arrivals changed; unverified = the rerun crashed, timed out or was not run, excluded); for -08 no shortlisted row from the future
flow.success: the frozen checker's own base checks all pass (recomputed); quality metrics are reported alongside
flow.counting: one attempt per trial; arrivals and checkpoints are not independent trials
